answer: Admissions each epoch fill a fixed seat count, rigid as a sonnet's set form, so rising demand pushes only into price. Each bidder submits a sealed velvet bid the protocol never unmasks; all bids burn and their aggregate sets one uniform clearing price. A farm lodging one bid per clone lifts its demand, dragging that price toward a higher horizon it pays on every seat it holds, so cost per identity climbs with its order size. The protocol never learns which hand holds a seat, yet its bulk bends the price; settlement reprices from committed bids and burns each, so no seat pools across farms.
